title: Normalized derived reduction and Roos restriction
statement: Fix coefficient data [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], a scheme $T$ and a clopen open $U$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-open-immersion]. Given normalized finite and completed ring restriction isomorphisms with exact module restriction, as in [def-sf-clopen-restriction-data], ordinary derived restriction commutes with finite scalar reductions, with their universal counits, actual termwise tensor quotients, transitions and units [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The comparisons fix sheafified pure tensors. Restriction preserves quotient-tower derived completeness [def-weil-derived-complete, def-weil-derived-limit] and the same residue Tor interval on every local site object [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. These conclusions are the fields of SfClopenCompleteRestriction for the supplied coefficient datum; they impose no lisse, affine or weak-contractibility hypothesis.

proof.text: Obtain the derived scalar and actual chain quotient isomorphisms with their pure-tensor and universal-counit normalizations. These comparisons apply to arbitrary complexes; no tower or chain coherence equations are assumed.

Prove the chain transition square after precomposing with the inverse quotient isomorphism. Apply the existing local pure-tensor extensionality lemma, compute the inverse comparison on each local pure tensor from its normalization, and apply the published quotient-transition formulas. The coefficient equation is d.transition evaluated on that section. This gives the transition square on every degree. Similarly, evaluate the chain unit on each section, use its formula x mapping to 1 tensor x and preservation of 1 by the coefficient isomorphism, and apply quotient_tensor to prove the chain unit square.

For P and exponent n+1 compose sfClopenLocalizationIso with the localized chain quotient isomorphism. Naturality of mapDerivedCategoryFactors moves a localized transition past the first isomorphism; functoriality and the chain transition equation then give consecutive-arrow naturality. NatTrans.ofOpSequence extends it to every arrow of the inverse system, and NatIso.ofComponents constructs the tower isomorphism. Its components are definitionally the prescribed quotient comparisons. The same localization naturality applied to the chain unit and then its unit equation proves the required augmented unit square.
Supply the preservation of derived completeness and the identical objectwise residue Tor interval, and assemble all fields of SfClopenCompleteRestriction.
